b.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's evening Outbox workflow, built on pinned data.

  1. Run Orders and Find customer once each, then click the pin icon in each Output panel.
  2. Edit the pinned Orders data and add a fourth order, HL-0074, with "total": 250000. Edit the pinned Find customer data so Iya Basira's "area" is empty. (Keep every item's customer_id matched to its order, or the link breaks.)
  3. Make the message survive the gap: {{ $json.area || 'your address' }}. Use ||, not ??, because an empty cell arrives as "", which ?? lets through.
  4. Run the workflow five times. Each run, Orders and Find customer show the pin, and the Outbox gets new rows.
order_idName in messageTotal shownEnds with
HL-0071Mrs Adebayo₦34,000Tuesday 6 Oct, Bodija.
HL-0072Mr Okafor₦4,000Tuesday 6 Oct, Ring Road.
HL-0073Iya Basira₦21,000Tuesday 6 Oct, your address.
HL-0074(its customer)₦250,000Tuesday 6 Oct, (their area).

Evidence: a screenshot of the canvas with both pin icons, the Executions list with five manual runs, and the Outbox rows. Every row must have a different name and its own order.
mistakes: Editing pinned data so an order's customer_id no longer matches any customer, then blaming the expressions.
Using ?? for the missing area, which lets an empty string through and leaves "Tuesday 6 Oct, ."
Checking only item 0 in the preview, so a .first() bug slips into the other messages.
Unpinning by accident (or re-executing a single node) so Google is called again mid-test.
b.pass: Both Sheets read nodes show pinned data, the Executions list shows five runs, and every Outbox row has its own customer's name, its own order number and a comma-formatted total, including ₦250,000 and a sensible fallback for the missing area.
b.redo: Send it back if any two rows share a name, a total shows unformatted or as an object, or the missing-area row breaks the message.

s.answer:
Worked example: five expressions written in Harvest Lane's Build message node, where $json is the customer and the order comes from $('Orders').item. Tested on item 0 (HL-0071, Mrs Adebayo, ₦34,000) and item 1 (HL-0072, Mr Okafor, ₦4,000), with today as Monday 5 October.

GoalExpressionItem 0Item 1
Tomorrow's date{{ $today.plus({ days: 1 }).toFormat('cccc d LLLL') }}Tuesday 6 OctoberTuesday 6 October
Total in naira₦{{ Number($('Orders').item.json.total).toLocaleString('en-NG') }}₦34,000₦4,000
7.5% VAT, rounded{{ Math.round(Number($('Orders').item.json.total) * 0.075) }}2550300
Local phone{{ $json.phone.replace('+234', '0') }}0803123456708029876543
Delivery line{{ Number($('Orders').item.json.total) >= 30000 ? 'Free delivery' : 'Delivery ₦1,500' }}Free deliveryDelivery ₦1,500

Notes for the log:

  • Tomorrow's date is the same for every item, which is correct. If you want each order's own day, use DateTime.fromISO($('Orders').item.json.delivery_date).toFormat('cccc d LLLL').
  • Number() guards against Sheets sending the total as text, which would make toLocaleString do nothing and the comparison unreliable.
  • To check item 1, use the arrows in the Input panel and read the preview under each field again. The phone numbers here are made up.
  • Nothing uses .first(): every order value follows the item link with .item. If item 1 ever shows ₦34,000, that is the first sign of a broken link.
mistakes: Formatting tomorrow's date from $now without .plus({ days: 1 }), so it shows today.
Using total.toLocaleString() on a value Sheets sent as text, so the comma never appears.
Writing VAT without Math.round, giving 2550.0000001 or 300.75-style results.
Reaching the order with $('Orders').first(), so item 1 shows item 0's total.
s.pass: The log has all five expressions, each with its output for two different items, the outputs match the expected values (₦34,000, 2550, 080…, Free delivery / Delivery ₦1,500), and no expression contains .first().
s.redo: Send it back if only one item was tested, any output is wrong for the second item, or .first() appears anywhere.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane adds a Riders sheet (area, rider_name, rider_phone): Musa covers Bodija, Kemi covers Mokola, Femi covers Ring Road, and nobody covers Agbowo yet.

Flow: Trigger → Orders → Find customer → Find rider (Get Row(s), filter area equals {{ $json.area }}, Settings: Always Output Data on, return only the first match so a second rider in one area can't double the message) → Build message → Outbox.

Build message now gets its input from Find rider, so $json is the rider:

Hello {{ $('Find customer').item.json.name }},
your Harvest Lane order {{ $('Orders').item.json.order_id }}
(₦{{ Number($('Orders').item.json.total).toLocaleString('en-NG') }})
arrives {{ DateTime.fromISO($('Orders').item.json.delivery_date).toFormat('cccc d LLL') }}.
{{ $json.rider_name ? 'Your rider is ' + $json.rider_name + ', ' + $json.rider_phone : 'Rider to be assigned' }}
OrderCustomerAreaLast line
HL-0071Mrs AdebayoBodijaYour rider is Musa, 0803…
HL-0072Mr OkaforRing RoadYour rider is Femi, 0805…
HL-0073Iya BasiraMokolaYour rider is Kemi, 0807…
HL-0075Chef TundeBodijaYour rider is Musa, 0803…
HL-0076Campus CaféAgbowoRider to be assigned

Which node each part reads from: name from Find customer (two steps back, via .item); order ID, total and date from Orders (three steps back); rider from Find rider ($json, the node directly before).

Submit: the five Outbox rows, the expression above, and that three-line explanation. All names and numbers are test data.
mistakes: Leaving Always Output Data off on Find rider, so the Agbowo order disappears instead of saying "Rider to be assigned".
Reading the customer with $json.name after adding Find rider, when $json is now the rider row.
Letting an area with two riders return two rows, so that customer gets two messages.
Testing with all five orders in the same one or two areas, so the three-area requirement isn't proven.
g.pass: Five test orders across at least three areas each produce one message with the right customer, order and rider, the no-rider area says "Rider to be assigned", and the learner states which node each expression reads from.
g.redo: Send it back if any message mixes customers or riders, the no-rider order is missing or broken, or the explanation of sources is absent.
